title: observability: propagate request-id + traceparent across streaming & OpenAI-compat, add structured logs and per-endpoint metrics tags
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: improve end-to-end observability for API surface (hosted and openai-compat gateway) by consistently propagating a request-id and W3C trace context through the gateway, streaming runtime, and worker processes. This change closes gaps where streaming responses dropped request-scoped metadata (request-id, traceparent, baggage) and adds structured logging fields and per-endpoint metric tags so teams can slice latency/cost/availability by route. Changes in this PR: - add Request-ID middleware that generates/accepts X-Request-Id and OpenTelemetry-compatible request_id header; persist in request context - propagate W3C traceparent and baggage headers through gateway -> runtime -> workers, ensuring spans can be correlated across services - attach request_id and trace ids to streaming frames and proxy frames so client SDKs (OpenAI-compatible and native) see the same ids for retries and debugging - add structured_log fields (request_id, trace_id, span_id, endpoint, model, route) to major log events and wire them into JSON logger used by prod - add per-endpoint metric tags for latency/cost/error metrics to Redwood metrics pipeline (route, method, model_variant) - update OpenAI compatibility layer to map OpenAI X-Request-Id / openai-id to our request_id and to return x-request-id in proxied responses - add unit + integration tests covering header propagation and a streaming integration test that asserts request_id is present on all frames - docs: update observability.md and openai-compat README with header mapping and troubleshooting guidance Checklist: - [x] Request-id middleware and tests - [x] Traceparent propagation and tracing tests - [x] Streaming frame metadata propagation - [x] Structured log additions - [x] Metrics tag plumbing + tests - [x] Docs and examples - [x] CI green Notes: There is a small behavioral change for customers using raw OpenAI-compatible responses: we now always emit x-request-id on responses (previously only sometimes set by upstream). This is backward-compatible but documented. See linked SUP ticket for a customer that requested deterministic request ids for debugging.
commits_summary: 5 commits: 1) add request-id middleware and context propagation; 2) propagate W3C traceparent and baggage through runtime worker boundary; 3) streaming: attach metadata to frames and update proxy to forward x-request-id; 4) add structured logging fields and tests; 5) metrics tags and docs updates
review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Nice end-to-end. Can you add a small note about privacy/PII when logging request metadata? We should avoid logging user prompt content in structured logs - only ids and route-level info.
Priya Shah: Responded - added explicit filtering in json_logger and added tests to assert prompt content is not emitted in structured fields.

Aisha Karim: Found a race where worker restart could drop baggage; suggested moving trace context onto the worker startup envelope. I pushed a follow-up commit to attach trace headers to worker start events.
Marco Li: CI flake on streaming test (flaky_streaming_frame_order) - reran CI and added a small backoff/ordering assert to stabilize the test. CI passed on rerun.
Ethan Brooks: Approved after addressing privacy note and adding the integration test confirming x-request-id is present on every streaming frame.
release_notes: Added consistent request-id and W3C trace propagation across gateway, streaming runtime, and OpenAI-compat proxy; structured logging fields and per-endpoint metric tags. This enables easier tracing of requests across services and slicing of latency/cost by route. Backwards-compatible: x-request-id is now always returned on proxied OpenAI-compatible responses.
